item.title: Cop31 talks go into overtime as debate rages over lack of fossil fuels in draft deal
item.description: African ministers say they ‘didn’t come here to beg’, with civil society groups calling it the ‘worst Cop ever’ Crucial climate talks headed into overtime on the last official day of the Cop31 UN summit as countries continued to argue over a draft deal that was silent on fossil fuels, with a host of other contentious issues complicating negotiations. Nearly 200 countries struggled to bridge their differences after two weeks of intense talks and impassioned speeches in Antalya, Turkey, about the effects of climate breakdown around the world, with a scheduled finish of Friday evening breached… Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.
item.dc:creator: Graham Readfearn, Fiona Harvey and Damien Gayle in Antalya, Turkey

item.description: El primer ministro británico, Andy Burnham , ha sido recibido este viernes en Bruselas con una escenografía espectacular por el presidente del Consejo Europeo, António Costa, y de la Comisión, Ursula Von der Leyen, que querían subrayar la importancia y el gran protagonismo que atribuyen a la relación con el Reino Unido a los diez años del Brexit. La reunión ha estado plagada de referencias a aquella separación y a las maneras de volver a reconstruir algunos de los puentes que se rompieron entonces. «Queremos las relaciones más estrechas con el Reino Unido. ¿Qué significa eso? Pues ya lo… Fuente: ABC España - Internacional.

item.title: Diez años después del Brexit, Reino Unido y la UE estrechan lazos con nuevos acuerdos
item.description: Diez años después del Brexit, las relaciones entre Reino Unido y la Unión Europea (UE) vuelven al centro del debate. Durante una cumbre celebrada este 20 de noviembre, el primer ministro británico, Andy Burnham, firmó acuerdos con el bloque europeo para facilitar el comercio y ampliar las oportunidades de movilidad para los jóvenes. Burnham, quien anteriormente había expresado su deseo de que Reino Unido regrese a la UE, aseguró que estos acuerdos contribuirán a reparar parte de los daños ocasionados por el Brexit. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Denmark expels Russian diplomat over plot to kill Ukraine rapper
item.description: Denmark’s foreign minister on Friday said Moscow’s defence attache in Copenhagen would be expelled after Russia was suspected of being behind an attempted assassination of a Ukrainian rapper. “We have just summoned the Russian ambassador to the ministry of foreign affairs and notified him of the government’s decision to expel the Russian defence attache from Denmark” within seven days, Lars Lokke Rasmussen told a news conference. He also added Denmark was mulling suspending Schengen visas for... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Agence France-Presse

item.title: UE y Reino Unido estrechan relaciones tras alcanzar un nuevo acuerdo
item.description: Los líderes buscan mejorar la relación tras el Brexit. El primer ministro británico, Andy Burnham, reconoció que al menos tres cuartos de la población birtánica piden mejorar las relaciones con la Unión Europea, su principal socio comercial. Entre los acuerdos alcanzados, tres en total, figura uno respecto a las normativas fitosanitarias, con lo que Reino Unido recuperará parte del mercado perdido luego de la imposición de nuevas medidas por la separación del bloque europeo. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: Luis Méndez Urich

item.title: En vivo: Trump ofrece una rueda de prensa tras reunirse con Xi y Putin
item.description: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, ofrece una rueda de prensa en la Casa Blanca este viernes, tras su regreso a Washington después de un viaje de cuatro días por Asia, durante el cual mantuvo una reunión —la primera de este tipo— con el presidente chino, Xi Jinping, y el presidente ruso, Vladímir Putin. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Hegseth refuerza cooperación en seguridad con Ecuador y Honduras en su gira por Latinoamérica
item.description: El secretario de Defensa de Estados Unidos, Pete Hegseth, concluyó su gira por Latinoamérica con visitas a Ecuador y Honduras. En Quito, durante su encuentro con el presidente Daniel Noboa, expresó su respaldo a la lucha contra el narcotráfico y los grupos armados ilegales, y aseguró que las Fuerzas Armadas estadounidenses están dispuestas a colaborar en el marco de la estrategia del Escudo de las Américas. Por su parte, en Tegucigalpa, el presidente Nasry Asfura afirmó que su país cuenta con el apoyo de Estados Unidos para combatir a las pandillas y el crimen organizado. Hegseth también… Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Sánchez y Feijóo, cara a cara en un debate marcado por la vivienda, la inmigración y la seguridad
item.description: El presidente del Gobierno de España, Pedro Sánchez, y el líder del opositor Partido Popular (PP), Alberto Núñez Feijóo, protagonizaron el 19 de noviembre un enfrentamiento político centrado en la crisis de vivienda, la inmigración y la seguridad ferroviaria, tras los dos graves accidentes de tren registrados este año. El encuentro fue el único debate cara a cara entre ambos dirigentes durante la campaña electoral, de cara a los comicios generales del próximo 29 de noviembre. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Hong Kong slams ‘biased’ US report accusing city of expanding security powers
item.description: Hong Kong has slammed an annual report by a US congressional commission that accused the government of expanding its security powers, including restricting media coverage of the Wang Fuk Court fire, the city’s deadliest blaze in decades. The Hong Kong government on Friday evening condemned the report issued by the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission (USCC) a day earlier, calling its accusations “biased slanders and smears”. It urged the United States to “discern facts from... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Directo España y el cara a cara entre Núñez Feijóo y Sánchez en el debate presidencial
item.description: A solo nueve días de las elecciones generales en España, el próximo 29 de noviembre, los dos líderes que encabezan las encuestas se enfrentaron en un debate. El líder del Partido Popular, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, y el presidente del Gobierno y candidato, Pedro Sánchez, chocaron el 19 de noviembre sobre la crisis de la vivienda, la inmigración y la seguridad ferroviaria, tras los dos graves accidentes de tren de este año. Nos amplió los detalles nuestra corresponsal, Marina Colorado. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.description: El escritor y exprimer ministro francés Dominique de Villepin presentó su candidatura a la Presidencia de Francia para 2027. Advierte de una guerra civil si la líder ultraderechista Marine Le Pen gana en los comicios y critica a Emmanuel Macron por ser un “presidente fantasma”. item.title: French ex-PM Villepin announces presidential run
item.description: France's former prime minister and foreign minister Dominique de Villepin, famed abroad for his excoriating 2003 denunciation of US plans for invading Iraq, said on Friday he was running for president. Villepin enters an already crowded field of candidates seeking to succeed President Emmanuel Macron, with polls pointing towards a possible run-off between frontrunner Marine Le Pen of the far-right National Rally (RN) and hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) veteran Jean-Luc Melenchon. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.description: El presidente salvadoreño habló sobre el despliegue de unos 2500 soldados en el país caribeño, donde la policía local lanzó un operativo que dejó 34 muertos y las fuerzas respaldadas por la ONU anunciaron una “nueva fase” Fuente: La Nación - El Mundo.

item.title: Spain’s political crossroads, Europe’s wider stakes: Spaniards to vote in key election
item.description: The stakes are high – not only for people in Spain, but also for Europe. On November 29, the country holds a parliamentary election that could see the end of the Socialist-led government and potentially a coalition between the right and the far right, in one of the EU’s biggest and most influential member states. It could also signal the end of Pedro Sanchez’s third term in office. Among other things, the prime minister may pay the political price for two shocking train crashes and the migrant crisis in Spain’s North African exclave of Ceuta. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.description: The joint pledge to reduce nuclear risk by the United States, China and Russia during their unprecedented three-way summit this week sends a positive signal on stability, analysts say, although they warn that there is little room for optimism without concrete measures. Nuclear arms control among the world’s three major nuclear powers – long sought by US President Donald Trump – failed to make it into the joint declaration after his talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President... item.description: Britain and the European Union went through a bitter divorce, then slowly began trying to rebuild their relationship. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham met the EU's top officials in Brussels on Friday for a summit he has described as a step towards undoing a decade of damage caused by the 2016 vote to leave the bloc. But how do the British public feel about closer ties with the EU – and, potentially, rejoining it? Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping urged visiting US President Donald Trump to do “the right thing” on Taiwan this week – a remark experts said suggested a push for further restrictions on US arms sales to the island. “The US must keep doing the right thing to avoid major setbacks in China-US relations,” Xi told Trump during their bilateral talks on Thursday at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit in Shenzhen, according to Beijing’s summary of the meeting. item.title: It’s just a song: Philippine leader laughs off debate over Apec welcome track Anak
item.description: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jnr has downplayed Beijing’s choice of music to greet him at the Apec summit, saying the debate about possible hidden meanings was overblown. A Chinese orchestra played the classic Philippine song “Anak”, which means child, when the Philippine presidential couple entered the hall for the welcome banquet in Shenzhen on Wednesday. The song, written by Freddie Aguilar, tells the tale of a young person’s rebellion against parental authority and subsequent... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Ghana's $60 million presidential jet purchase sparks controversy
item.description: Ghanaian President John Mahama is facing growing criticism over his government's recent purchase of a $60 million presidential jet. While in opposition, Mahama had criticised similar plans by the previous administration. The government in Accra is now defending the purchase, pointing to the country's improved economic situation. It argues that the question was never whether the ageing presidential aircraft should be replaced, but rather when the timing would be right. FRANCE 24's Justice Baidoo reports. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Was the historic Shenzhen summit a political win or humiliation for Putin?
item.description: The world watched with bated breath Thursday as the presidents of China, Russia and the United States met for 90 minutes for an unprecedented trilateral summit in Shenzhen. Each leader came to the negotiating table with their own motivations. But Russia's Vladimir Putin was seen as walking away worse off than his counterparts, with some media outlets reporting the Kremlin leader was "humiliated" during the talks. item.title: Rare EU-UK summit as Andy Burnham seeks to mend Brexit damage
item.description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and the EU's top officials were set to announce deals to ease trade and youth mobility at a Brussels summit Friday, billed as a first step in a push to rebuild ties after Brexit. But in a potential spoiler for Burnham's "reset", Brussels said the deals coming into force would be conditional on reaching an agreement to cut university fees for EU students in Britain. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Rochelle Ferguson Bouyahi tells us more. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: 'Coalition of the Willing': Ukraine's allies meet in Berlin after Trump-Putin-Xi talks
item.description: Ukraine's allies met Thursday for a "Coalition of the Willing" summit in Berlin with President Volodymyr Zelensky to stress solid wartime support for Kyiv and to push for a European role in any future peace talks. The meeting – co-hosted by the leaders of Germany, France and Britain – was being held shortly after unprecedented three-way talks in China between US President Donald Trump, Russia's Vladimir Putin and China's Xi Jinping. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Spain's leaders clash over corruption, economy in tense election debate
item.description: Spain's Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez acknowledged making "mistakes" as he faced off with his main conservative rival in a key debate on Thursday before an election next week that could leave the far right on the cusp of power. The pair clashed over the economy, housing, immigration, corruption, foreign policy, as well as policies towards women, repeatedly interrupting each other during the live televised showdown. Iraqi officials had accused the group of running a smuggling ring that siphoned off hundreds of millions ​of dollars' worth of ‌state-owned oil. Under the deal brokered by senior Shi'ite political leaders to avert a confrontation, government ⁠forces were expected to move into the group's stronghold of Jurf al-Sakhar on Friday. item.description: France’s former conservative prime minister Dominique de Villepin, who served as former president Jacques Chirac’s foreign minister during the country’s steadfast opposition to the US-led invasion of Iraq in 2003, formally launched his presidential campaign Friday.
